title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 246
paragraphs: The Nile, then, besides that part of its course within Egypt, is known for as far as a four months' journey by river and land: that is the number of months found by reckoning to be spent travelling from Elephantine to these “Deserters”; and the river runs from the west and the setting sun. But what lies beyond that no one can clearly say, for this land is desert by reason of the burning heat.
